title: feat: context window management
description: This PR introduces a token-aware context window management system to the codebase, making it easier to ensure prompts and conversation histories fit within the token limits of various LLMs. It adds the `ContextWindow` class and related utilities, exposes them in the package API, provides extensive tests, and updates documentation and user guides to explain their use.

title: feat: Ollama detection
description: This PR adds first-class support for local Ollama model detection and registration. It introduces new utilities to automatically discover, profile, and register Ollama models, making them available alongside other model providers.

title: feat: add model capability profiles
description: This PR introduces a new "Model Profiles" capability registry, which provides a structured way to register, query, and display information about supported language models and their features.

title: feat: add `eval_model_update()`
description: This PR introduces a new utility function, `eval_model_update()`, to the evaluation framework, allowing users to easily compare persona performance across two model versions and detect regressions. The function is fully integrated into the API, documented in the user guide, and covered by new tests.

title: feat: scorecard to GT table
description: This PR introduces two new public utility functions, `scorecard_table` and `sweep_table`, for rendering evaluation results as polished, color-coded tables using Great Tables. These functions are now part of the public API, are documented in the user guide, and are covered by comprehensive tests. The changes make it significantly easier for users to visualize and share evaluation and sweep results in notebooks, docs, and HTML reports.

title: feat: eval suite
description: This PR adds support for local and multi-persona evaluation workflows and updates Anthropic model references throughout the codebase and documentation. The biggest changes are the addition of new evaluation scripts, Makefile targets for running evaluations, and updates to model naming conventions for Anthropic models.

title: feat: persona-aware default guards
description: This PR enhances the persona system by enabling personas to declare default guardrails (such as PII detection and disclaimers) that are automatically applied when loading a persona with `persona_pack()`. The PR also adds a new `resolve_guards` utility for declarative guard instantiation. On top of this, we update persona definitions to specify their default guards. Docs and tests are updated to cover these new features. Finally, users can now opt out of default guards when loading a persona.

title: feat: eval system
description: This PR adds evaluation and scoring functionality and makes the relevant evaluation classes and functions available for import. The main changes are the inclusion and documentation of evaluation-related APIs, which will allow prompt evaluation, scoring, and regression detection.

title: feat: guardrails
description: This PR introduces a guardrail system that allows developers to add modular validation and moderation checks to chatbot interactions. We add here guardrail-related APIs to the public interface, integrating guardrails into the chatbot message flow, and provide utilities for testing and statistics.

title: feat: autotest pathways
description: This PR is focused on testing the automated pathway feature in ChatBots. The focus is on testing with the `autotest_pathways()` function. It introduces a new user guide page with explanations and code examples, making it much easier for users to understand, implement, and analyze pathway adherence testing.

title: docs: rework some articles and improve flow
description: This PR makes significant improvements to the docs, focusing on clarifying the advantages of the `PromptBuilder` system, reorganizing the user guide for better usability, and updating code examples for accuracy and consistency. The changes also include improvements to section names and titles, as well as minor content and formatting updates across several documentation files.

title: feat: `Pathways` visualization
description: This PR provides a way to produce visualizations for any `Pathways` object. The generated HTML is helpful for validating pathway logic before implementation, debugging complex branching and reconvergence scenarios, and documenting conversation flows for reference.

title: feat: tool use through the Tool Box
description:
This PR provides a pretty comprehensive tool system that allows for creating, testing, and using AI tools with Talk Box conversations. Some of the features include:

- easy tool creation with `@tb.tool` decorator
- `ToolContext` with conversation history
- built-in testing framework for tool validation
- pre-built library of common tools (the Talk Box Tool Box)
- integration with Talk Box attention-focused prompts
- comprehensive observability and debugging

title: feat: add domain-specific vocabulary system
description: This PR introduces `VocabularyTerm` for defining specialized terminology with synonyms and translations, integrated through `PromptBuilder.vocabulary()`. This enables LLMs to correctly interpret domain-specific language across industries and languages, preventing misinterpretation of terms that may have different meanings in different contexts.

title: feat: incorporate prompt text formatting with 100-character line width limits
description: This PR Implements smart text wrapping that preserves code blocks, maintains numbered list alignment, and handles complex indentation while respecting line width constraints. This also includes comprehensive test coverage with many tests covering edge cases and different integration scenarios.

title: feat: state extract ID from `desc=` in `.state()`
description: This PR implements a shorthand syntax for defining state IDs in the `.state()` method, allowing users to write `"id: description"` format instead of separate `id=` parameters.

title: feat: add conversational Pathways feature
description:
This adds the Pathways feature, which helpers to provide conversation flow guidance while maintaining the flexibility to adapt to natural conversation patterns. Here's an example of how it works in practice:

```python
import talk_box as tb

onboarding = (
    tb.Pathways(
        title="Customer Onboarding",
        desc="Welcome new customers and set up their accounts",
        activation="New customer signs up",
        completion_criteria="Customer is ready to use the platform",
        fallback_strategy="If customer needs help, provide direct support contact"
    )

    # === STATE: welcome ===
    .state("Welcome customer and collect basic information", id="welcome")
    .required([
        "customer's full name",
        "email address",
        "company or organization name"
    ])
    .success_condition("Customer feels welcomed and basic info is collected")
    .next_state("setup")

    # === STATE: setup ===
    .state("Configure account preferences", id="setup")
    .required([
        "password created and confirmed",
        "notification preferences selected",
        "timezone configured"
    ])
    .optional(["profile photo uploaded", "team member invitations"])
    .success_condition("Account is fully configured")
    .next_state("tour")

    # === STATE: tour ===
    .state("Provide guided tour of key features", id="tour")
    .required(["main features demonstrated", "first task completed"])
    .success_condition("Customer understands how to use core functionality")
)

# See the generated prompt fragment
print(onboarding)
```

The Pathways object can be used with ChatBot via PromptBuilder:

```python
bot = (
    tb.ChatBot()
    .model("gpt-4")
    .system_prompt(
        tb.PromptBuilder()
        .persona("helpful customer support agent")
        .pathways(support_pathway)
    )
)

bot
```

title: feat: chat component
description:
This PR introduces a new React-based chat interface that provides a fairly modern UI alongside the existing browser chat. The update includes documentation, packaging, and code changes to support the new interface, as well as improvements to LLM conversation context handling and persona management.

Updated documentation and user guides to include installation instructions, usage examples, and feature descriptions for the React chat interface. Modified `pyproject.toml` to include React-related files in the package, and added dependencies for FastAPI, Uvicorn, and requests to support the React chat server. Also, updated package configuration to ensure all necessary web components are included for deployment.

The `ChatBot` interface is extended to support `show("react")`, and this includes error handling and integration logic for launching the React chat server. The LLM conversation context handling is improved by replaying previous messages to maintain history for more coherent responses.

title: feat: add Attachments class
description:
This PR introduces support for file attachments, enabling users to include and process documents, images, and other files in LLM conversations. The changes span documentation, public API, and core logic, making file attachment workflows accessible, well-documented, and robust for both single-turn and batch interactions.

Also added a new user guide that details workflows, supported file types, best practices, and HTML display features for file attachments. The changes provide a good foundation for file-based analysis workflows in the library.

title: feat: autotest to-be-avoided topics for a ChatBot
description:
This PR introduces a new testing and validation framework for chatbot behavior, with a focus on compliance with 'avoid topics' constraints. We add here new testing utilities and enhance the chatbot builder API for introspection.

Importantly, we strengthen the language used in system prompts and prompt builders to enforce topic avoidance (it was too weak before, only leading to topic indirection at best).
